defaultValue: Every friendly market with a spaceport has an Extra Systems bay in its main menu. Each upgrade has levels; every level makes its stats a little stronger, and hull quality multiplies the result.

fieldDescription: Levels each upgrade can be bought up to with credits or materials. Changing it rescales existing upgrades: level 5 of 10 becomes level 5 of 20, which is half as strong.
Extra levels past the maximum. Each one costs a story point on top of its price. 0 turns overclocking off.
Multiplies the effect of every upgrade. 2 doubles every bonus; 0.5 halves it. Reductions never go below their floor, so supply use and the like cannot reach zero.

defaultValue: Every hull has a quality that multiplies the effect of its upgrades. Shipyards (Heavy Industry, Orbital Works and their modded equivalents) can raise it; each improvement costs more than the last. A ship's starting quality is fixed the first time the bay works on it.

fieldDescription: Each hull starts with its own quality between the two values below. Switch off to start every hull at 100%.
The worst a hull can roll. 1 means 100%.
The best a hull can roll. 1 means 100%.
The most a shipyard can raise a hull's quality to. 2 means 200%: every upgrade works twice as hard.

defaultValue: Augments are rare devices with an effect of their own. They turn up in salvage and can be fabricated at markets with Orbital Works. A ship holds as many as its hull size allows.

fieldDescription: Augment slots on a capital ship.
Switch on to make removal destroy the augment instead of returning it to your cargo, like the original Extra System Reloaded.

defaultValue: Prices follow each hull's value, so a capital costs far more to upgrade than a frigate. Shipyards and your own colonies give discounts. Paying with materials or Industrial Evolution components is cheaper than paying credits.

fieldDescription: Multiplies the price of every upgrade level.
Multiplies the price of every hull quality improvement.
Multiplies the price of fabricating an augment.
Share of a level's price paid back when you remove it. 0.5 means half.
